title: [Audit] 🔎 Elasticsearch Data Access
description: What data was read, by whom, through which transport action — including system indices.

config.description: All Elasticsearch audit events in range.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-elasticsearch" | STATS `Elasticsearch events` = COUNT(*)

config.description: Distinct index families named in audited requests — the rows Top index families and the matrix would list with no cut. A data stream and its backing indices are one family, as is a run of dated daily indices, and system and hidden indices count once per area (.alerts*, .slo*, .kibana*…), the groups the ⚠️ table names. Wildcard and date-math expressions (*, -*, <…{now/d}>) are patterns, not indices, and are left out.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices IS NOT NULL AND (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IN ("indices:data/read/esql/search_shards", "indices:data/read/esql/data"))) | STATS BY attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices | WHERE LOCATE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, "*") == 0 AND NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE "<*" | EVAL family = REPLACE(REPLACE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, """^\.ds-""", ""), """[-.]?\d{4}[.-]\d{2}[.-]\d{2}(-\d+)?$""", "") | EVAL family = CASE(LEFT(family, 1) == ".", CONCAT(REPLACE(family, """^(?:\.ds-)?(\.(?:alert-actions|[^-._]+)).*$""", "$1"), "*"), family) | STATS `Index families` = COUNT_DISTINCT(family)

config.description: Distinct Elasticsearch transport actions (cluster:*, indices:*), with shard-level copies and ES|QL sub-steps folded away — the same actions Top transport actions lists, all traffic.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NOT NULL | STATS BY attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action | WHERE NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/esql/*") | STATS `Distinct actions` = COUNT(*)

config.description: ES|QL queries submitted — one per query, not per shard or sub-step. Includes the queries these dashboards run to draw themselves. Equals the indices:data/read/esql row in Top transport actions. At a range ending now, panels beside each other can differ by a few: audit events land a few seconds after they happen (this page's own queries among them), and each panel is read at a slightly different moment.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action == "indices:data/read/esql" | STATS `ES|QL queries` = COUNT(*)

config.description: Requests touching dot-prefixed system and hidden indices (.kibana*, .security*, .slo-*, .alerts-*), counted once per index named. Backing indices of ordinary data streams (.ds-logs-…) are not system data and are left out, as are shard-level copies of a request.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices IS NOT NULL | MV_EXPAND attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices | WHERE ((attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".*" AND NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-*") OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-.*") AND (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*") | STATS `System index access` = COUNT(*)

config.description: Authorization denials. Sustained non-zero values mean a misconfigured client or a probe.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.action == "access_denied" OR attributes.event.action == "anonymous_access_denied" | STATS `Access denied` = COUNT(*)

config.title: Data access over time by action family
config.description: Every Elasticsearch request that names a transport action, by kind of action — all traffic, the searches and ES|QL these dashboards run among the reads. Shard-level copies, ES|QL sub-steps and the search an async search runs for itself are folded away so a request counts once, and authentication and connection events (which name no action) are left out, so it sums to less than the Elasticsearch events tile. The legend gives each family's total, so a family too small to see as a bar is still counted; Lens leaves the bucket still filling at the right edge out of those totals (up to half an hour at 24h), so they run behind the bars and the tiles. A stretch with no bars means no audited Elasticsearch request in that span — on a wide range that includes the time before the project's audit stream began.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NOT NULL | STATS n = COUNT(*) BY time = BUCKET(@timestamp, 75, ?_tstart, ?_tend), attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action, request = attributes.elasticsearch.audit.request.name | WHERE NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/esql/*") AND NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action == "indices:data/read/search" AND COALESCE(request, "-") == "") | EVAL family = CASE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read*", "read", attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/write*", "write", attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:admin*", "index admin", attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "cluster:admin/xpack/security*", "security admin", attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "cluster:admin*", "cluster admin", attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*:monitor*", "monitor", "other") | STATS events = SUM(n) BY time, family | SORT family

config.title: Who reads which index family · up to 10 identities
config.description: The 10 busiest identities across the top, and the 25 index families they read most down the side; cell colour is audit events on a log scale, teal (fewest) through blue and purple to pink (most), and the line above the matrix says how many of each it shows. A data stream and its backing indices are one family, as is a run of dated daily indices, and system and hidden indices are one family per area (.alerts*, .slo*, .kibana*…), the groups the ⚠️ table names; wildcard and date-math expressions are left out. A blank cell means that identity did not touch that family in range — or touched it too little to be among the 500 busiest identity/family pairs. Events counts a request once per index it names: shard-level copies and the ES|QL engine's per-shard steps name the same indices again and are left out, so it is the same count as Top index families. An identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its opaque id. Cells keep a heatmap's size and pack to the top left when only a few identities or families are in range, so a sparse window draws a small matrix with its legend under it, not a few cells adrift in the panel.

config.title: Top index families by events · 14 at most
config.description: The busiest index families, all traffic; the Index families tile counts every one, so the rest are beyond this list. Identities is how many distinct identities touched the family, and Busiest identity is the one with the most events against it — over a quiet hour the list is often only the audit stream itself, read by the identity these dashboards run as. A data stream and its backing indices are one row, as is a run of dated daily indices, and system and hidden indices are one row per area (.alerts*, .slo*, .kibana*…), as in the ⚠️ table: one request naming ten alert indices is one .alerts* row, not ten. Events counts a request once per index it names, so a system area's events per identity are the ⚠️ table's; shard-level copies and the ES|QL engine's per-shard steps name the same indices again and are left out (an ES|QL query counts once, by the step that resolves its indices). Wildcard and date-math expressions are left out. The same count the matrix beside it colours. A Busiest identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its opaque id.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices IS NOT NULL AND (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IN ("indices:data/read/esql/search_shards", "indices:data/read/esql/data"))) | STATS n = COUNT(*) BY attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices | WHERE LOCATE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, "*") == 0 AND NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE "<*" | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), index = REPLACE(REPLACE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, """^\.ds-""", ""), """[-.]?\d{4}[.-]\d{2}[.-]\d{2}(-\d+)?$""", "") | EVAL index = CASE(LEFT(index, 1) == ".", CONCAT(REPLACE(index, """^(?:\.ds-)?(\.(?:alert-actions|[^-._]+)).*$""", "$1"), "*"), index) | STATS n = SUM(n) BY index, actor | EVAL k = CONCAT(TO_STRING(n + 1000000000000), actor) | STATS events = SUM(n), actors = COUNT(*), top = MAX(k) BY index | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 14 | EVAL busiest = SUBSTRING(top, 14) | EVAL busiest = CASE((LENGTH(busiest) == 20 AND busiest RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT busiest RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(busiest, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), busiest) | KEEP index, busiest, actors, events

config.title: Top transport actions · 13 at most
config.description: The busiest Elasticsearch transport actions with their request class, all traffic — the searches and ES|QL reads these dashboards run included, since reads are what this page is about. The Distinct actions tile counts every action; the rest are beyond this list, and an action sent with two request classes is two rows. Shard-level copies, ES|QL sub-steps and the search an async search runs for itself are folded away, so a request counts once. Identities is how many distinct identities sent the action; Request "—" means the event named no request class. At a range ending now, panels beside each other can differ by a few: audit events land a few seconds after they happen (this page's own queries among them), and each panel is read at a slightly different moment.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NOT NULL | STATS n = COUNT(*), seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action, request = attributes.elasticsearch.audit.request.name | WHERE NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/esql/*") AND NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action == "indices:data/read/search" AND COALESCE(request, "-") == "") | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), request = CASE(request IS NULL OR request == "", "—", request) | STATS events = SUM(n), actors = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor), last_seen = MAX(seen) BY attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action, request | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 13

config.title: Denied requests by identity · newest 10 at most (empty = good)
config.description: Who was refused, newest first: one row per identity, with the action and index of its most recent denial, how many distinct actions and indices it was refused on, and its denials in range. When more identities were refused than the panel has rows, the last row (“N other identities”) holds the rest — their denials and newest Last seen — so the Denials column always adds up to the Access denied tile. On index "—" is a cluster-level request, with no index to count; <anonymous> with action "—" is an HTTP call that carried no credentials, refused before it named an action. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email. An empty panel means nothing matched in the time range, which is the healthy state; any row here is worth reading.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.action == "access_denied" OR attributes.event.action == "anonymous_access_denied" | STATS events = COUNT(*), seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), k = CONCAT(TO_STRING(seen), "|", COALESCE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action, "—"), "|", COALESCE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, "—")) | STATS events = SUM(events), last_seen = MAX(seen), latest = MAX(k), actions = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action), indices = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices) BY actor | INLINE STATS ids = COUNT(*), recent = VALUES(last_seen) | EVAL cut = MV_MIN(MV_SLICE(MV_SORT(recent, "DESC"), 0, 8)) | EVAL actor = CASE(ids > 10 AND last_seen < cut, "~rest", actor) | STATS events = SUM(events), last_seen = MAX(last_seen), latest = MAX(latest), actions = MAX(actions), indices = MAX(indices), folded = COUNT(*) BY actor | EVAL actor = CASE(actor == "~rest", CONCAT(TO_STRING(folded), " other identities"), actor) | EVAL latest_action = CASE(folded > 1, " ", MV_SLICE(SPLIT(latest, "|"), 1)), latest_index = CASE(folded > 1, " ", MV_SLICE(SPLIT(latest, "|"), 2)), actions = CASE(folded > 1 OR actions == 0, null, actions), indices = CASE(folded > 1 OR indices == 0, null, indices) | KEEP actor, latest_action, latest_index, actions, indices, events, last_seen | SORT last_seen DESC | LIMIT 10 | EVAL actor = CASE((LENGTH(actor) == 20 AND actor RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT actor RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(actor, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), actor)

config.title: ⚠️ Who touched system and hidden indices · newest 25 at most (empty when none in range)
config.description: Who touched system and hidden indices — Kibana internals, the security index, alerting and SLO data — one row per identity, newest first: the index groups it touched (.alerts*, .slo*, .kibana*…), the kinds of transport action (read, write, index admin, monitor…), how many real indices, and its requests in range, which add up to the System index access tile when every identity is in view. The Discover session below names each index and action. Backing indices of ordinary data streams (.ds-logs-…) and shard-level copies of a request are left out. Expected from Kibana and platform automation; unexpected from anyone else, and a write from anyone else is worth a look. An identity that touched many groups wraps onto a second line rather than cutting the list short. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email. Often empty over the default hour on a healthy project; widen the time range to see older rows. The table holds more rows than the panel shows: scroll it for the rest.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices IS NOT NULL | MV_EXPAND attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices | WHERE ((attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".*" AND NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-*") OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-.*") AND (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*") | STATS n = COUNT(*), seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), area = CONCAT(REPLACE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, """^(?:\.ds-)?(\.(?:alert-actions|[^-._]+)).*$""", "$1"), "*") | EVAL family = CASE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read*", "read", attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/write*", "write", attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:admin*", "index admin", attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "cluster:admin/xpack/security*", "security admin", attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "cluster:admin*", "cluster admin", attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*:monitor*", "monitor", "other") | STATS events = SUM(n), indices = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices), groups = VALUES(area), kinds = VALUES(family), last_seen = MAX(seen) BY actor | EVAL groups = MV_CONCAT(MV_SORT(groups), ", "), kinds = MV_CONCAT(MV_SORT(kinds), ", ") | KEEP actor, groups, kinds, indices, events, last_seen | SORT last_seen DESC | LIMIT 25 | EVAL actor = CASE((LENGTH(actor) == 20 AND actor RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT actor RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(actor, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), actor)

config.title: Raw system index requests · newest 1,000 at most (empty when none in range)
config.description: The raw events behind the table above: the newest 1,000 requests against a system or hidden index, one row per index named, newest first — so a single request that names ten alert indices is ten rows with one timestamp here, and one .alerts* entry in the table above. It stops at 1,000, so it can hold fewer rows than the System index access tile counts — the "1,000 results" above the grid is that cap, not the total. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email. Often empty over the default hour on a healthy project; widen the time range to see older rows.
